notes: Batch AA (cefixime, cefalexin, cefuroxime oral, azithromycin, doxycycline, nitrofurantoin). All quotes checked with lib/text.mjs quoteFound (same as fetchtext --check). BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). SUBSTITUTE PRODUCT: cefixime - no UK SmPC exists for the clinic's 100 mg/5 mL oral suspension or 400 mg capsule (emc search by ingredient and trade name; MHRA Products index shows only 200 mg film-coated tablets). The UK 200 mg tablet SmPC (emc-15047) is used for both clinic forms and this is stated in each formulation note. Its 'not recommended under 10 years' statement is about the 200 mg tablets; it was applied as an 'avoid' age rule to the capsule form only (my interpretation, flagged in the rule text). It gives no paediatric dose, so the suspension has no paediatric dosing. BETA-LACTAM CROSS-ALLERGY (reaction filters only where the SmPC distinguishes them): cefuroxime 4.3 contraindicates use after SEVERE hypersensitivity (e.g. anaphylaxis) to other beta-lactams and 4.4 gives caution for NON-SEVERE reactions, so its rules use reactions [immediate-severe, severe-cutaneous] (contraindicated) and [immediate, delayed] (caution); including severe-cutaneous under 'severe hypersensitivity' is an interpretation (the SmPC's example is anaphylaxis only). Cefixime and cefalexin SmPCs give caution for penicillin hypersensitivity without distinguishing reaction type, so those rules have no reaction filter. NITROFURANTOIN RENAL: both UK SmPCs say eGFR below 45 but print the unit as 'ml/min' / 'ml/minute'; MHRA DSU (2014) says eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2. Measure recorded as eGFR, max 45 (exclusive). The eGFR 30-44 exception (MHRA: short course 3 to 7 days with caution for resistant lower UTI; Macrodantin-type SmPC 4.4 agrees) is a separate caution rule (eGFR min 30, max 45). The Mylan SmPC 4.3 also contraindicates 'increased serum creatinine' and the Macrodantin-type SmPC 4.2 says contraindicated 'in patients with renal dysfunction'; recorded as a contraindicated condition rule on renal-impairment (applies when eGFR is not entered). DOXYCYCLINE CHELATION: the UK capsule SmPC (and the dispersible tablet SmPC emc-6262, checked but not cited) only say 'Dosages should be maximally separated' - no hour interval is given, so none is stated. Rules made for groups antacid, polyvalent-cation, iron-preparation, calcium-preparation and magnesium-preparation with the same concern text so they merge. DOXYCYCLINE AGE: 'should not be used' under 8 years -> avoid (4.2, not 4.3); 8 to <12 years 'carefully justified' -> caution. AZITHROMYCIN QT: SmPC 4.4 says use with caution in QT prolongation, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, bradycardia, arrhythmia, severe cardiac insufficiency and with QT-prolonging medicines; SPS QT page says for macrolides 'Do not prescribe in people with a history of QT interval prolongation, ventricular arrhythmia, or significant electrolyte disturbance' -> kept as separate SPS 'avoid' condition rules (conflict recorded). SPS also says macrolides raise QTc by <5 ms and no ECG is needed when used alone without risk factors. The current Zithromax SmPC (Jul 2026) lists antacids as causing no clinically relevant change in exposure, so no antacid rule was made for azithromycin. CONFLICTS: (1) doxycycline pregnancy - SmPC 4.3 contraindicated vs BUMPS (can be used if a doctor recommends; avoided after ~13 weeks); (2) doxycycline breastfeeding - SmPC 4.3 contraindicated vs SPS 'can be used with caution' (short courses); (3) nitrofurantoin pregnancy - one SmPC 4.3 contraindicates at term (labour and delivery), the other says 'best not' just before/during delivery and 'can be used' if prescribed; BUMPS avoid in 3rd trimester; (4) nitrofurantoin breastfeeding - one SmPC 'must be temporarily avoided' only if infant has (suspected) G6PD/erythrocyte enzyme deficiency, the other 'can be used', SPS 'with caution'; (5) nitrofurantoin paediatric doses differ (3 mg/kg/day from 3 months vs 3 to 6 mg/kg/day for girls 5 to 12); (6) the Mylan nitrofurantoin 4.8 table lists idiopathic intracranial hypertension, short-lived alopecia and superinfection as 'very common', which conflicts with the other SmPC (frequency not known) and looks like a table error - those frequencies were not used; (7) cefixime 'should not be used in pregnancy or nursing mothers unless essential' (avoid) vs BUMPS cephalosporin leaflet (most studies show no harm). NOT FOUND: no SPS breastfeeding page for cephalosporins (SPS search and breastfeeding index checked; URL guesses 404), so cephalosporin breastfeeding uses SmPCs only; no MHRA DSU specific to cefixime, cefalexin, cefuroxime, azithromycin (other than the hydroxychloroquine-macrolide DSU) or doxycycline. Doxycycline 4.8 table columns are lost in the fetched text, so no frequencies are claimed. NOT MAPPED (no master-list match or would mislead): aminoglycosides in the cefalexin nephrotoxicity warning (master list has only topical gentamicin products); probenecid, ergot derivatives, digoxin, colchicine, ciclosporin, dabigatran, isotretinoin, methoxyflurane, phenytoin, barbiturates, magnesium trisilicate, typhoid vaccine. Group 'hepatotoxic' (doxycycline rule) currently has no members in any batch. Nitrofurantoin-urinary alkaliniser rule targets sodium-bicarbonate-potassium-citrate; its 'alkaliniser' status is quoted from the potassium citrate SmPC emc-4922 (same id/URL as batch Z). BRAND PRESCRIBING: no UK source says to prescribe any of these by brand. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second check, see audit/Z-AA.md): nitrofurantoin condition rule on renal-impairment (contraindicated) replaced by a rule on new condition raised-serum-creatinine, because the engine links renal-impairment to GFR below 60 and so flagged a false contraindication at eGFR 45 to 59 (both SmPC 4.3 sections qualify renal dysfunction with eGFR below 45); azithromycin and nitrofurantoin added to group hepatotoxic (their SmPC 4.4 hepatotoxicity warnings report fatal hepatic failure or necrosis, the same basis as clarithromycin, ciprofloxacin and co-amoxiclav in batch E); doxycycline NOT added (only a 4.8 list entry and rare abnormal hepatic function in 4.4), integrator to decide; penicillin-allergy caution rules for cefixime and cefalexin no longer list group:beta-lactam (it also matched cephalosporin allergies under a penicillin label; those are covered by the contraindicated cephalosporin rules); cefuroxime severe-reaction rule keeps severe-cutaneous and now says this is an interpretation; cefixime suspension under-10 info rule added.
